record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: Let C be the collection of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold M that are topologically conjugate to a structurally stable diffeomorphism, and let E be topological conjugacy restricted to C. Is E Borel reducible to equality?

evidence.quote: Question 1.5 (Foreman). Let C be the collection of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold M that are topologically conjugate to a structurally stable diffeomorphism. Let E be the relation of topological conjugacy restricted to C. Is E Borel reducible to ≈ (equality relation)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold and let $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ denote the Polish space of $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms of $M$ (with the $C^\infty$ topology). A diffeomorphism $f \in \mathrm{Diff}(M)$ is called structurally stable if there exists a neighborhood $U$ of $f$ in $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ such that for every $g \in U$ there is a homeomorphism $h : M \to M$ with $h \circ f = g \circ h$. Two diffeomorphisms $f, g \in \mathrm{Diff}(M)$ are topologically conjugate, written $f \sim_{\mathrm{top}} g$, if there exists a homeomorphism $h : M \to M$ such that $h \circ f = g \circ h$.

Let
$$C = \{ f \in \mathrm{Diff}(M) : f \text{ is topologically conjugate to some structurally stable diffeomorphism} \},$$
and let $E$ denote the equivalence relation $\sim_{\mathrm{top}}$ restricted to $C \times C$.

Recall that an equivalence relation $E$ on a standard Borel space $X$ is Borel reducible to equality on a standard Borel space $Y$ (written $E \leq_B {=}_Y$) if there is a Borel function $\varphi : X \to Y$ such that for all $x, x' \in X$, $x\, E\, x'$ if and only if $\varphi(x) = \varphi(x')$.

Question: Is $E$ Borel reducible to equality?
artifact.category_tag: Borel equivalence relations in smooth dynamics
artifact.status_search_result: The question is attributed to Foreman as an open problem in the area of anti-classification results for smooth dynamical systems. While Foreman and collaborators have proven that topological conjugacy on all of Diff(M) is not a Borel equivalence relation, no published resolution of the restriction to the structurally stable conjugacy class C is evident in current literature; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Anti-classification results for smooth dynamical systems
status_evidence.snippet: Topological conjugacy of diffeomorphisms is shown not to be a Borel equivalence relation; restrictions to nice subclasses remain to be analyzed.
status_evidence.claim: Foreman-Gorodetski work establishes anti-classification for general Diff(M) but does not resolve the structurally-stable restriction.

status_evidence.title: Classification problems from descriptive set theory
status_evidence.snippet: Survey lists Foreman's questions on Borel reducibility of topological conjugacy restricted to structurally stable diffeomorphisms as open.
status_evidence.claim: The question is recorded as an open problem in current surveys.
